crops.name: Apple
crops.overview: Ireland's most important tree fruit, with hundreds of heritage varieties.
crops.ireland: Excellent — choose scab-resistant varieties for wetter western areas.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

planting.seed_rate: Bare-root Nov–Mar or container all year

conventional.N: Low: 30–60 kg N/ha/yr equivalent; mulch with compost
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Compost or well-rotted FYM mulch in spring; seaweed; wood ash or permitted potassium sulphate for K; lime only if pH low.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Water young trees in dry spells for the first 2–3 years; mulch. Established trees rarely need irrigation in Ireland.

harvest.signs: Fruit lifts and twists off easily; pips brown
harvest.storage: Pick by the variety season; store sound fruit cool (3–5°C), dark, slightly humid; check weekly.

conventional.pests: Scab and canker are the big problems in Irish wet weather; also powdery mildew, codling moth, aphids, sawfly, bitter pit (calcium). Fungicide programmes and pheromone traps per label.
conventional.weeds: Keep a 1 m weed-free circle with mulch or herbicide.

organic.pests: Choose scab/canker-resistant varieties (many Irish heritage apples), open-centre pruning for airflow, clear fallen leaves, prune out canker, pheromone traps and grease bands, encourage birds and earwigs. Sulphur and potassium bicarbonate are permitted for mildew/scab under EU organic rules — check with your body.

crops.rotation: Do not replant apples where apples grew (replant disease) — use a new site or change soil.

crops.name: Nectarine
crops.ireland: Under cover only in most of Ireland.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

planting.window: Nov–Mar, warm wall or under cover
planting.seed_rate: Bare-root Nov–Mar or container all year

conventional.N: Low: 30–60 kg N/ha/yr equivalent; mulch with compost
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Compost or well-rotted FYM mulch in spring; seaweed; wood ash or permitted potassium sulphate for K; lime only if pH low.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Water young trees in dry spells for the first 2–3 years; mulch. Established trees rarely need irrigation in Ireland.

harvest.storage: Short shelf-life; eat fresh, freeze, bottle or jam.

conventional.pests: Silver leaf and bacterial canker (prune only in summer), peach leaf curl, brown rot, plum moth, aphids, birds.
